content.whyJoin:
The Design Masterprize (DMP) is a global design award program celebrating excellence in product, graphic, and communication design. Organized by the Farmani Group, which runs award programs across design, architecture, photography, and the arts, DMP provides a global stage for designers across a broad spectrum of disciplines and experience levels.

The 2026 edition features 29 top categories spanning product, graphic, and communication design, including automotive, packaging, UI/UX, branding, typography, advertising, and web design. Entries are judged online through a custom voting system, with distinctions including Best of Best, Winner, Honorable Mention, and Official Entry.

Winners receive the DMP trophy for designs of the year, certificates and badges for sub-category winners, inclusion in the yearly DMP Book of Design, and a feature in the Winners Gallery. All winner benefits are included in the submission fees, with no hidden costs.
content.whoShouldApply:
This award is open to designers, engineers, and creators of all experience levels and ages from any country, participating as individuals or companies. It welcomes work from product design, graphic design, communication design, advertising, digital media, and related fields.

Entries can be conceptual, in-progress, or previously awarded in other competitions, so both emerging and established designers can participate. Submissions are accepted in 29 categories, and each entry is evaluated independently in its chosen category.

This call suits designers and studios looking for global recognition, PR campaigns, and networking with creative minds across the world.

faq.question: Who can enter the Design Masterprize?
faq.answer: DMP is open to designers, engineers, and creators of all experience levels and ages from any country. Individuals and companies can participate, and there are no age or experience restrictions for any category.

faq.question: What categories are available?
faq.answer: The 2026 edition features 29 top categories spanning product, graphic, and communication design, including automotive, beverage and food, consumer electronics, packaging, UI/UX, typography, advertising, and web design.

faq.question: How much does it cost to enter?
faq.answer: Entry fees start at €225 for professionals and €50 for students in the early entry period. Additional categories for the same entry receive a 30% discount, and discounts are available for earlier deadlines.

faq.question: What are the key deadlines?
faq.answer: The early entry deadline with a 25% discount is March 31, 2026. The extended early entry is May 18, 2026 with a 20% discount, the regular deadline is June 30, 2026 with 10% off, and the final deadline is July 31, 2026.

faq.question: What do winners receive?
faq.answer: Designs of the year receive the DMP Trophy. Sub-category winners receive winner certificates, badges, inclusion in the yearly DMP Book of Design, and a feature in the Winners Gallery. Best of Best is awarded to the highest scoring winners in each main category.

faq.question: Can previously awarded works be submitted?
faq.answer: Yes. DMP welcomes exceptional designs regardless of previous accolades. Works that have received awards in other competitions can be submitted, and there is no limit on the number of entries.

submissionGuide.detail: Navigate to the registration page on the Design Masterprize website and follow the step-by-step instructions to create your entry, providing your personal or company details.

Review the 29 category descriptions and choose the category that best represents the primary focus of your design. Entries can be submitted to multiple categories with a 30% discount for additional categories.
Provide project details, images, and a brief description. Entries can be conceptual, in-progress, or previously awarded works.
Complete payment through Stripe, which accepts all major credit and debit cards. Payment is required for jury consideration, and entries cannot be edited once paid.
Entries are reviewed by editors and judged online by expert jurors through a multi-stage voting system, with Best of Best, Winner, and Honorable Mention distinctions announced afterward.
